metaDescription: Five compact trim routers under $150, compared on speed range, soft start, base clarity, collet size and the bit set that decides what you can cut.
expertTake: The SKIL RT1324-00 is the pick for most woodworkers, because a 6.5 amp motor with a six-step dial from 10,000 to 35,000 rpm and a spindle lock covers laminate, edge profiling and hinge mortises. The WEN RT1460 is the value pick, thanks to a soft-start motor and a transparent base. Skip a trim router if you need to cut large profiles in hardwood, because a 1/4 inch collet and a small motor are not built for big bits.
introParagraphs: A trim router is a small, single-handed router built for edge work: rounding over a tabletop, trimming laminate flush, cutting hinge mortises and shaping small profiles. The headline horsepower and rpm on the box matter less than the base, the collet and how smoothly the motor starts.

This guide explains what a spending cap of $150 buys, what you give up against a full-size router, and how to read speed and collet specs. Our top picks are above, with full reviews below. Prices move, and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: SKIL RT1324-00 6.5 Amp Corded Trim Router, 10,000-35,000 RPM
products.description:
The RT1324-00 pairs a 6.5 amp motor with a speed range from 10,000 to 35,000 rpm on a six-step dial. A wide range matters because router bit speed should match the bit: a small bit cuts cleanly at high speed, while a larger bit needs a lower speed to avoid burning the wood and overloading the collet. Most small routers run at a single speed, so a dial is a real advantage.

An integrated spindle lock holds the shaft in place so you can change bits with one wrench, which saves time and prevents dropped bits. A 6.5 amp motor gives enough power for edge work in hardwood, though it is not designed for deep profiles. Compared with the WEN RT1460, the SKIL has more amps and a wider speed range, while the WEN has a soft start.

Check that the collet nut tightens firmly and that the bit shank is clean, since a poorly seated bit is the main cause of vibration. Keep the base smooth and clean of pitch. For hinge mortises, set the speed in the middle of the range and make two shallow passes, because a single deep pass in oak bogs a 1/4 inch bit and burns the cut. A template guide bushing system, bought separately, turns it into a repeatable mortising tool.
products.bestFor: General edge work, laminate trimming and small profiles in hardwood.
pros: Six-step dial from 10,000 to 35,000 RPM matches speed to the bit
6.5 amp motor handles edge work in hardwood
Spindle lock allows single-wrench bit changes
Recognized brand with easy parts and bit access
cons: No soft start, so the motor jolts at switch-on
1/4 inch collet limits bit shank size
Not built for deep cuts or large profiles

products.name: WEN RT1460 6 Amp Handheld Laminate Trim Router, 12,000-30,000 RPM
products.description:
The WEN RT1460 uses a soft-start motor, meaning the speed ramps up gradually when you pull the trigger instead of snapping to full rpm. A soft start prevents the torque jolt that twists a small router in your hand and spares the motor windings from a hard inrush. It is a quiet quality feature that most budget routers skip.

The adjustable straight base has 1-5/8 inches of travel and a one-inch scale marked in 1/16 inch steps, so you can set cut depth without a separate gauge, and a transparent base lets you see the bit and the line. The speed range of 12,000 to 30,000 rpm is narrower than the SKIL's, and the motor is a quarter amp smaller. Against the TEENO, the WEN has the soft start and a more traditional design.

Use a sharp bit and make light passes, since a trim router is not designed for deep cuts. Keep the collet clean and replace it if bits begin to slip. On laminate, a flush-trim bit with a bearing rides the substrate edge and trims the overhang in one pass, but keep the router moving left to right against the bit rotation to avoid grabbing. Keep a spare collet nut, since overtightening can crack it.
products.bestFor: Laminate trimming and light edge work where a soft start helps control.
pros: Soft-start motor prevents the torque jolt at switch-on
Scale marked in 1/16 inch steps helps set depth
Transparent base shows the bit and the cut line
12,000 to 30,000 RPM suits most small bits
cons: Narrower speed range than the SKIL
6 amp motor is slightly weaker than the 6.5 amp rivals

products.name: TEENO 1.25 HP 6.5 Amp Compact Palm Router, 6-Speed
products.description:
TEENO's palm router combines a 1.25 horsepower copper motor, equal to 800 watts or 6.5 amps, with a six-speed dial and an impact-resistant clear base. A clear base is not a gimmick, since it lets you see the bit and the cut line without leaning over the tool, which matters when you follow a pencil line on a laminate edge.

The tool stands 7.9 inches tall and 3.5 inches wide, a compact size that fits one hand, and the motor power puts it on par with the SKIL. The tradeoff is brand support and published detail: the listing does not state a spindle lock or soft start. Against the AVID POWER 630W, the TEENO has more motor and a clear base.

Make sure the router sits flat on the work, since a rocking palm router digs in. Use a 1/4 inch collet bit with a full shank, and replace the collet if bits slip. Because the body is slim, it sits comfortably in one hand but can tip if you lean on one side, so keep the base flat against the work and use two hands for the final trimming pass. Dust blows around fast, so wear eye protection.
products.bestFor: Buyers who follow layout lines and want visibility of the cut.

1.25 HP motor matches the SKIL for power

products.name: AVID POWER 630W 5.3 Amp Compact Router with 3 Guide Modes
products.description:
AVID POWER offers a 630 watt motor, about 5.3 amps, spinning at 35,000 rpm, with three guide modes and a fixed base. Guide modes let you use a rub bearing, a straight edge or an edge guide to control the cut, which makes the router more versatile for edge trimming. A fixed base is the classic design for a trim router, simple and rigid.

The motor is the smallest in the group, so it is better suited to laminate, softwood and light profiles than to deep cuts in hardwood. Against the SKIL and TEENO, which have 6.5 amp motors, the AVID gives up about 20 percent of the current rating, but it ships with trim bits, which saves a purchase. The listing does not mention a variable-speed dial, so you run at a fixed high speed.

A fixed-speed router at 35,000 rpm should be used with small bits only. Keep the base clean and use a sharp bit for the cleanest cuts. Use the guide modes with care, since a rub bearing follows a template exactly, which means an error in the template transfers to the work. A router also throws chips at high speed, so a pair of safety glasses is not optional.
products.bestFor: Laminate and softwood edge trimming with bits included.
pros: Three guide modes give flexible edge control
Trim bits included for a first project
35,000 RPM gives a smooth finish with small bits
Fixed base is simple and rigid
cons: 5.3 amp motor is the weakest in the roundup

products.name: TwoWin 800W Compact Palm Router with 6-Piece Carbide Bit Set

specList.label: Bit set
specList.value: 6 tungsten carbide bits in wooden box

products.description:
TwoWin ships an 800 watt palm router with a six-piece tungsten carbide bit set in a wooden box, a 1/4 inch collet and an edge guide. An 800 watt motor is equivalent to about 6.7 amps, comparable to the SKIL and TEENO. A six-bit set covers common edge profiles, so a beginner can start work without buying separate bits.

The adjustable depth system sets cut depth, and the edge guide holds the router at a fixed distance from an edge. The tradeoff is that the listing gives little detail on the speed controls or a spindle lock, and the brand is lesser known. Against the AVID POWER, it has a stronger motor and more bits.

Carbide bits cost more but stay sharp far longer than steel bits, which is a real value in a kit. Keep the bits in the box, check the shank before each use and replace any bit with chips on the cutter. Check that the edge guide is square to the base before you cut, because a slightly crooked guide gives a bevel along the whole edge. Store the bits in the box with their shanks up so the cutters do not clip each other.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a router and a set of carbide bits in one box.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Router bits need different speeds depending on diameter, with small bits cutting best at high speed and larger bits needing slower speeds. The SKIL offers 10,000 to 35,000 rpm in six steps, and the WEN offers 12,000 to 30,000. A fixed-speed router like the AVID's 35,000 rpm is limited to small bits. As a rule of thumb, bits under 1/2 inch run best between 24,000 and 35,000 rpm, while larger bits belong at the low end of the dial.

A soft start ramps the motor up smoothly, which prevents the torque jolt that twists a small router in your hand. The WEN RT1460 lists a soft-start motor. Without it, hold the router firmly and clear of the work when you switch it on. A hard start can also spin the bit into the work at the first instant, so keep the bit clear until it reaches speed.

A 1/4 inch collet grips a 1/4 inch shank bit, which suits trim work, and a 1/2 inch collet is for larger routers. All five here are 1/4 inch routers. A worn collet lets bits slip, so replace it at the first sign. Insert the shank at least three quarters of its length into the collet, and never bottom it out.

A clear base lets you see the bit and the cut line, and a flat base prevents rocking. The TEENO has an impact-resistant clear base, and the WEN has a transparent base. A base that rocks digs into the work. A tall base also raises the router's center of gravity, which makes small trim routers tippy on narrow edges.

A trim router needs enough power for small bits in hardwood. The SKIL and TEENO at 6.5 amps and the TwoWin at 800 watts lead, and the AVID at 630 watts trails. Do not use a trim router for deep cuts, since the motor overheats. Light passes, no more than 1/8 inch deep, protect both the motor and the bit.

A bit set saves a purchase, and carbide bits stay sharp longer. The TwoWin ships six carbide bits and the AVID ships trim bits, while the SKIL and WEN ship with few. Plan to buy a quality bit or two regardless. A flush-trim bit and a roundover bit are the two bits to buy first for most work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed control
howWeEvaluated.description: We began with speed range and steps. The SKIL's six-step dial from 10,000 to 35,000 RPM led. We treated a dial as a significant safety and quality feature, since a wrong speed burns wood and wears bits.

howWeEvaluated.title: Start and base
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at soft start and base design. The WEN's soft start and the TEENO's clear base stood out.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared amps and watts. The SKIL and TEENO at 6.5 amps led, followed by the TwoWin at 800 watts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bit set and accessories
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered what is in the box. The TwoWin's six carbide bits and edge guide stood out. Bits included were counted only if they were carbide or stated as usable.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted recurring themes such as collet slip and base rocking. Lesser known labels were scored cautiously for parts support.

Budget tiers here are relative and include the value of the bits in the box.

cards.label: Variable speed
cards.text: The SKIL, WEN and TEENO let you match speed to the bit, which prevents burning in hardwood.

cards.label: Fixed or high speed
cards.text: The AVID runs at a fixed 35,000 rpm. It suits small bits only.

howToChoose.note: Pick variable speed if you use different bits. Pick fixed for simple trimming.

howToChoose.intro: Base design affects accuracy more than motor power on a trim router.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A flush-trim bit, a smooth base and light passes. A soft start helps control the router at the edge.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WEN RT1460 is the best fit with its soft start. The SKIL suits mixed work.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You route daily or need a plunge base. A pro compact router with a fixed and plunge base outlasts these.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim edges occasionally. The AVID or TwoWin covers that.

maintenance.why: Pitch on a bit causes burning and vibration. Clean with a bit cleaner or solvent, and replace any bit with a chipped cutter.
A worn collet lets bits slip under load, which is dangerous. Replace it at the first sign, and never tighten it without a bit installed.
Pitch makes the base drag. Wipe it clean.
Dust clogs vents. Compressed air keeps the motor cool.
A nicked cord is a hazard. Replace damaged cords.

faq.q: Do I need a trim router or a full-size router?
faq.a: A trim router suits edge work and small profiles in one hand. A full-size router handles large bits and deep cuts, and many shops own both.

faq.q: What does $150 buy in a trim router?
faq.a: A 5.3 to 6.5 amp corded palm router with a 1/4 inch collet. You give up a plunge base and brushless motors. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: Why does my router burn the wood?
faq.a: Usually the speed is too high, the bit is dull or you are moving too slowly. Slow the speed, use a sharp bit and make lighter passes at a steady feed rate.

faq.q: Can a trim router cut large profiles?
faq.a: No. A small motor and a 1/4 inch collet are not suited to large bits.

faq.q: Which bit should I buy first?
faq.a: A flush-trim bit and a roundover bit cover most work.
Yes. Wear eye and ear protection and a dust mask, and clamp the work. Keep your hands clear of the bit path and wait for the bit to stop before setting the router down.
